mission.title: Select a mission
mission.lunarSummary: Build a crewed ship, fly a compressed Earth departure, and work on the Moon.
mission.marsSummary: Spend more performance on a longer transfer and look for a water-related sample.
mission.stationSummary: Reach Earth orbit and complete a repair spacewalk.
mission.asteroidSummary: Fly an uncrewed science craft toward a real near-Earth asteroid scenario.
mission.rescueSummary: Intercept a stranded crew and bring them aboard.

brief.title: Mission briefing

obj.lunar: Reach lunar orbit, deploy a rover, photograph the surface, collect a sample, and transmit the data.
obj.mars: Reach the Mars scenario, deploy a rover, photograph the terrain, investigate a water clue, and transmit.
obj.station: Rendezvous in Earth orbit, inspect the station, repair a solar panel, restore communications, and check life support.
obj.asteroid: Approach 2012 TC4 in the scenario, measure it, estimate composition, and file a report.
obj.rescue: Find the distress signal, intercept, dock, and recover the crew.

brief.disclaimer: Ranges come from JPL Horizons. Flight time in the simulator is compressed and is not a real transit time.

build.title: Spacecraft construction
build.clear: The current parts satisfy this mission.
build.tradeoff: A heavier engine raises thrust and propellant flow, and usually lowers specific impulse. The performance figure uses the rocket equation. It is a gameplay calculation, not a NASA launch approval.
build.boosterHint: Choose “No booster” or add a booster you must separate in flight.
build.hangar: Engineering hangar. Part choices change mass, propellant, cost, and the flight.
build.modelNote: Drag to inspect. This spacecraft is gameplay geometry, not a NASA vehicle or photograph.
build.bayNote: The hangar is a game environment, not a NASA facility photograph.

flight.title: Manual flight
flight.cockpit: Cockpit display. The 3D view is in this browser, not a headset.
flight.hintPad: Start the engines, raise thrust, then pitch the nose from vertical toward the suggestion. W and S pitch, A and D yaw, Q and E roll.
flight.hintAscent: Pitch over from vertical toward the suggestion. Yaw and roll change where the thrust points. Insertion needs altitude, downrange speed, and a nose near the horizon.
flight.hintCorrection: Hold pitch on the target and thrust between 28% and 62%. Stabilization will hold the attitude you set.
flight.hintCoast: Downrange speed closes the transfer. Engage autopilot to fly the approach, or land it yourself once the destination frame begins.
flight.hintApproach: This pass uses destination-relative speed. Pitch, thrust, and reaction control are the same controls as launch. A landing is confirmed only after a safe contact.
flight.failLift: The vehicle did not climb away from the pad.
flight.failFuel: Propellant ran out before the required speed.
flight.failPitch: The vehicle climbed without building orbital speed.
flight.failHeat: The temperature index exceeded the training limit.
flight.failAbort: Emergency abort. The engines are shut down and the flight is closed.
flight.failLanding: Touchdown speed or attitude was outside the safe limit. The landing was not confirmed.
flight.failDock: The docking pass was too fast or poorly aligned. Contact was not confirmed.
flight.failAsteroid: Relative speed was too high for this low-gravity rendezvous. Contact was not confirmed.
flight.failPath: The transfer did not reach the destination corridor.
flight.compressed: Kinematics run at 24× so a launch fits a demonstration. The cockpit speed control multiplies that clock. Attitude has inertia, thrust spools toward the slider, and fuel burns with simulation time. This is not a certified trajectory.
flight.simSpeedHint: 1× normal, 2× fast, 5× very fast, 10× maximum. Motion, fuel, and mission timers stay on the same clock.

pilot.lead: Practice pitch, yaw, roll, thrust, and reaction control on a booster flight before you commit a real mission.
pilot.rebindHint: Click a command, then press the key you want. Escape cancels.
pilot.axes: Nose up {{up}}, nose down {{down}}, yaw left {{left}}, yaw right {{right}}. Pull the stick back to raise the nose.

lesson.start: Press Start engines. Thrust stays at zero until the engines are running.
lesson.throttle: Move the thrust slider, or hold the thrust-up key, until the engine is above 60%.
lesson.pitch: Push the stick forward, or hold nose-down, until pitch passes 12°. Pitch is the nose moving toward the horizon.
lesson.yaw: Move the stick sideways, or hold yaw, until the nose is at least 8° left or right.
lesson.roll: Roll left or right until the craft has rotated about 12° around its long axis.
lesson.sas: Turn stabilization on. It damps the rotation and holds the attitude you release.
lesson.rcs: Turn RCS on, then tap a translation control. Those jets nudge the craft without using the main engine.
lesson.stage: Separate the booster. The button appears only while a booster is still attached.
lesson.done: You have flown each control. Keep practicing, or leave and start a real mission. This flight is not scored.

autopilot.relative: Landing speed is relative to the destination. An asteroid or docking pass must be much slower than a planetary landing.
autopilot.hasControls: Autopilot is flying pitch, yaw, roll, and thrust.
autopilot.assistNote: Assisted mode steadies the trajectory while you keep the engine switch.
autopilot.safe: Switch modes any time the flight has not failed and final contact has not started.
autopilot.warnEngine: The engine is not producing thrust. Take manual control.
autopilot.warnFuel: Propellant is too low for the remaining maneuver. Thrust is being conserved.
autopilot.warnHeat: Temperature is high. Thrust is being reduced.
autopilot.warnSpeed: Closing speed is still high for this destination. A correction is in progress.
autopilot.warnPath: The ascent is leaving the corridor. Guidance is trying to bend it back.
autopilot.warnImpact: Contact speed or attitude was outside the safe limit. The landing was not confirmed.
autopilot.blockFailed: Autopilot cannot engage after the flight has ended.
autopilot.blockDone: The vehicle has already finished the arrival.
autopilot.blockEngine: The engine has failed. Fly manually.
autopilot.blockFuel: Not enough propellant to hand the vehicle to the autopilot.
autopilot.blockHeat: The vehicle is too hot to engage the autopilot.
autopilot.blockContact: Final contact is underway. Finish it in the mode already selected.
autopilot.blockHandoff: The autopilot could not keep this trajectory safe. You have the controls.

surface.title: Destination operations
surface.hudNote: Oxygen, energy, health, and spare parts are the mission resources already being simulated.
surface.medical: Educational indicators only. Not a medical measurement.

incident.title: Incident
incident.lunar: Lunar dust is coating the rover radiator.
incident.mars: A dust storm is cutting solar input.
incident.station: A suit caution appears during the panel repair.
incident.rescue: The intercept is using propellant faster than planned.
incident.safeResult: The cautious procedure spent a spare part and stabilized the system.
incident.riskResult: Pushing ahead saved time and left the system degraded.

report.title: Mission report
report.recSuccess: The design and the piloting both left margin. Repeat the flight with a tighter propellant budget.
report.recPartial: Review the failed objective and the resource that ran low before the next attempt.
report.recFail: Return to construction or fly closer to the suggested pitch.

assistant.title: Mission Control Assistant
assistant.rule: Rule-based assistant. No external AI service is connected.
assistant.pad: Hold for engine start. Suggested pitch begins near vertical.
assistant.pitch: Your pitch is outside the suggested corridor.
assistant.fuel: Propellant is getting low for the phase you are in.
assistant.energy: Energy use is ahead of production.
assistant.correction: A trajectory correction is armed. Match the target pitch and a mid thrust setting.
assistant.heat: Temperature index is climbing. Reduce thrust or follow the suggested pitch.
assistant.separate: Booster propellant is spent. Separate it or you will carry dead weight.
assistant.fatigue: The crew is showing fatigue. Schedule rest before the next task.

nasa.title: NASA data and sources
nasa.lead: No Challenge 13 resource pack was in the project folder. The items below were retrieved directly from NASA and JPL services on 14 November 2026. They are not labeled as the official challenge attachment list.
nasa.notUsed: GMAT, NTRS, and NASA 3D models were not integrated. A third-party challenge atlas is not treated as the official resource list.
nasa.gravity: Moon surface gravity quoted by Horizons
nasa.notPhoto: Planets in the 3D view are colored meshes. They are not NASA photographs.
nasa.notHardware: Rocket mass, cost, and thrust in the builder are original gameplay values.
nasa.images: Four public-domain photographs from the NASA Image and Video Library are shown on the home and mission cards. Credits are listed above.
nasa.a1: Specific impulse and propellant mass use the ideal rocket equation with standard gravity 9.80665 m/s².
nasa.a2: Powered-flight motion is integrated at 8× so the demonstration stays short.
nasa.a3: Propellant flow follows real seconds, not the compressed kinematic clock.
nasa.a4: A single correction burn stands in for the full transfer. Real lunar and Mars transfers take days.
nasa.a5: Crew bars are classroom indicators, not medical data.
nasa.missing: Supabase, WebRTC, LiveKit, and VR are not configured and are not presented as working.

tutorial.title: Tutorial
tutorial.s1: Pick a language, then enter the local demo. Nothing here requires an account.
tutorial.s2: Choose Lunar Exploration and build a ship. Red margins mean the design cannot lift the mission.
tutorial.s3: Inspect every checklist row. On the pad, pitch over along the suggestion, then fly the correction burn yourself.
tutorial.s4: On the surface, complete each task, answer the incident, and read the report. Reset the demo from Settings.

about.title: About
about.body: CALL OF SPACE is a student mission-design game for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, aimed at the Space Mission Design Game challenge. It is not a NASA product and it does not provide certified flight, medical, or mission-planning advice.
about.sources: NASA data used in this game

train.gateTitle: How do you want to start?
train.gateLead: This choice changes guidance only. Missions, construction, and flight stay available either way.
train.academyLead: Six modules use the same ship, checklist, flight model, and surface tasks as a real mission. Replay any module.

mode.recruitText: A six-module program with Mission Control beside the real screens.
mode.experiencedText: Enter the game with hints off. Turn them back on from Settings or the field manual.
mode.freeText: Look through the features with hints available and no required module order.

goal.command: Learn the menu, the resource meters, and how a mission states its limits.
goal.engineering: Install the balanced engine and the medium tank. The hangar stats are the live craft.
goal.planning: Read the lunar limits, then load a design that clears every hold.
goal.launch: Inspect every checklist row, then start the engines in the flight model.
goal.navigation: Set the correction pitch and thrust the flight model actually accepts.
goal.surface: Finish the lunar surface tasks and resolve the incident with the cautious choice.

skill.command: Read a mission budget and a red hold.
skill.engineering: Install an engine and a tank.
skill.planning: Match a design to the mission limits.
skill.surface: Complete surface tasks and protect the crew.

command.intro: Home is Play, then Solo or Multiplayer. Tutorial, Leaderboard, Progression, About, Help, Settings, and Quit game stay in the menu. A mission shows a budget and a required performance figure. Those are gameplay limits, not a NASA flight plan.
command.meters: These bars are the same kind of meters used for propellant, energy, and oxygen.
command.qBudget: Which number is the lunar mission budget in this game?
command.qRed: A red margin on the hangar means:
command.redHold: The design cannot carry this mission yet.
command.redOk: The design is cleared for launch.
command.redPhoto: The picture is a NASA photograph of the ship.
command.done: You can read the command screen. The next module uses the hangar.

engineering.intro: The hangar shows a gameplay model, not a NASA vehicle. Categories match the real slots: engine, tank, structure, power, communications, navigation, science, crew, and life support. Installing a part changes mass, propellant, thrust, cost, and the holds.
engineering.askEngine: Install the balanced engine. A heavier engine raises thrust and also cost and propellant flow.
engineering.askTank: Install the medium tank. Propellant capacity on the right is the live figure.
engineering.done: The craft changed because those parts are installed. Continue uses the same builder as a mission.

planning.intro: Lunar Exploration asks for budget {{budget}}, performance {{dv}} km/s, and communications {{comms}}. A crewed lunar flight also needs life support and a science instrument.
planning.empty: An empty ship fails the real readiness checks. Load the lunar training design, then confirm it.
planning.done: The training design is inside the limits: cost {{cost}}, performance {{dv}} km/s. Those figures come from the game model.

launch.intro: Every checklist row has to be inspected. Launch stays locked while a hold remains. Propellant then burns in real seconds while the trajectory clock runs faster.
launch.result: Engines are lit in the flight model. Propellant left {{fuel}} t. Altitude {{altitude}} km.
launch.fuelNote: Thrust spends propellant. If the tank reaches zero before the required horizontal speed, the flight ends.

nav.intro: W and S change thrust. A and D change pitch, and the sliders do the same. During the correction, the model accepts a pitch within 6° of 48° and thrust from 28% to 62% for 3.2 seconds.
nav.ask: Set that correction. Full thrust is not accepted for this burn.
nav.done: That setting matches the correction the flight screen will ask you to hold.

surface.intro: There is no separate rover to drive. Science is the surface task list: deploy, photograph, sample, and transmit. Oxygen, water, food, and energy are the simulated reserves. The cautious incident spends a spare part. The risky one cuts energy and oxygen. Crew rest, water, and food change the crew bars.

coach.brief: Read the objective and the distance note, then open the hangar.
coach.pickEngine: Choose an engine first. The balanced engine is the training choice for the Moon.
coach.fixHolds: Red lines are the checks this design still fails. Change the part that line names.
coach.buildReady: The design clears this mission. Continue to the checklist.
coach.inspect: Inspect each row. A row you have not opened still blocks launch.
coach.launch: The checklist is clear. Start the engines, then pitch toward the suggestion. A test flight is available before you commit.
coach.incident: An incident is open. The cautious choice spends a spare part and keeps the crew safer.
coach.tasks: Finish each surface task. Data rises when a task is recorded.
coach.surfaceReady: The tasks are done. Complete the mission to write the report.

hint.hangar: Select a category, then a part. The spacecraft in the center is gameplay geometry. Mass, propellant, power, and cost update from that choice.
hint.cockpit: Start the engines, then set thrust. Nose up and down are W and S. Yaw is A and D. Roll is Q and E. The stick and the RCS pad do the same things with the mouse.
hint.fuel: Propellant falls while the engines burn. The bar is the propellant you still have for this flight.
hint.eva: Before the tasks, watch oxygen and energy. At zero oxygen the task buttons stop.
hint.crew: Health falls when oxygen is low. Water, a meal, and rest move the crew bars. They are classroom indicators, not medical data.

miss.budget: That number belongs to another mission. The lunar budget is 1100.
miss.red: Red is a hold, not a clearance and not a photograph credit.
miss.engine: The exercise asks for the balanced engine. The other engines are real parts, and their stats are already on the right.
miss.tank: The exercise asks for the medium tank so the later training design stays consistent.
miss.plan: The design still has a hold. Load the lunar training design, then confirm.
miss.correction: Pitch must sit within 6° of 48°, and thrust must sit between 28% and 62%.

manual.controls:
Home: Play opens Solo and Multiplayer. Test flight opens a free practice rocket. Tutorial opens this program.
Flight: G starts the engines and C stops them. The slider or Shift and Ctrl set thrust from 0% to 100%. W and S pitch the nose up and down. A and D yaw. Q and E roll. T holds attitude. R toggles reaction control, and I K J L U O translate. B separates a booster. Backspace arms the abort, then confirms it.
The stick, translation pad, and buttons do the same commands with the mouse. Keys can be changed in the cockpit or in Settings.
Surface: each task button records that objective. Drink, meal, and rest are the crew actions.
manual.build:
Pick a category, then a part. One part occupies each slot. The training design uses the balanced engine, no booster, medium tank, medium frame, command module, solar array, high-gain antenna, basic navigation, science camera, a crew of two, and basic life support.
Mass, propellant, thrust-to-weight, cost, and communications are gameplay values.
manual.resources: Propellant is spent by thrust. Energy comes from the power part minus the parts that draw power. On the surface, oxygen, water, and food fall over time. A closed-loop life support slows the oxygen loss. Spare parts are spent by the cautious incident response.
manual.launch: Inspect every checklist line. Launch stays disabled while any line fails or has not been inspected. After ignition, pitch over from vertical toward the suggestion. Insertion needs altitude, horizontal speed, and a nose that is not straight up.
manual.nav: Pitch is the angle from vertical. Yaw swings the nose left or right and sends thrust off the downrange line. Roll spins the craft on its long axis and rotates how the stick and the reaction jets act. The suggested pitch changes with altitude. The correction burn is a short stand-in for a multi-day transfer: hold about 48° and a mid thrust setting. Stabilization holds the attitude you release. Coast then finishes the demonstration flight.
manual.objectives: Each mission card lists a budget and a required performance. The briefing states the objective. Surface tasks are the objectives you still have to record. The report lists what you completed.
manual.crew: A crewed mission needs a crew part and life support. Health, fatigue, hydration, nutrition, stress, and sleep are simulated bars. Rest reduces fatigue. Water and food raise hydration and nutrition and spend those reserves.
manual.eva: Station repair uses the same surface screen. Oxygen and energy are the reserves to watch. This game does not include a separate rover to drive. Deploy, photograph, sample, and transmit are the science actions.
manual.trouble:
The ship will not climb: thrust is too low, or pitch is not lifting you off the pad.
Propellant hits zero early: the tank is small or thrust stayed high for too long.
Correction will not complete: pitch is outside 6° of 48°, or thrust is outside 28–62%.
Checklist launch is disabled: a row is still a hold or has not been inspected.
Surface tasks are locked: an incident is waiting, or oxygen has reached zero.
Red text in the hangar names the failed check.
manual.glossary:
Budget — gameplay cost limit for the selected mission.
Performance — ideal-rocket change in velocity, in km/s, from the parts you installed.
Thrust-to-weight — liftoff thrust compared with the weight of the stacked vehicle.
Pitch — nose angle from vertical.
Corridor — a score for how closely pitch followed the suggestion.
Hold — a failed readiness check.
Propellant — the tank mass the engines can burn.
EVA — activity outside the spacecraft. Here it is the surface task list.
Correction — the short burn that stands in for the long transfer.
These are game terms. They are not certified flight definitions.
